transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess I’m here because my sleep just hasn’t been good for a long time. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I’ll come home exhausted and fall into bed, and then I wake up at every little noise in the house. And I’m usually up before the alarm, feeling like I didn’t really rest at all. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but it’s been wearing on me.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried around bedtime, or does your mind tend to race when you’re trying to fall asleep?

I’m not sure I’d call it anxiety exactly… I mean, maybe I think about things a little, like anyone does, but I haven’t really noticed my mind racing in a big way when I’m trying to fall asleep. It’s more that sleep just doesn’t seem to stay solid, if that makes sense.
Do you often wake up feeling unrefreshed, like your sleep didn’t really restore you, even if you were able to fall asleep easily?

Yes… pretty often, honestly. Even if I fall asleep okay because I’m so tired, it’s like it doesn’t really count. I wake up to little sounds, and then I’m usually awake before the alarm, and I don’t feel restored. I don’t know if I’m explaining that right, but it’s been going on a long time.
Do you find yourself feeling unusually sleepy during the day, even after a full night's sleep?

Some days, yes… I mean, I try to push through it, and I don’t want to overstate it, but even when I’ve been in bed long enough, the sleep feels so broken that I wake up like I never really rested. So during the day I can feel pretty worn out, like I’m running on very little.
Can you describe what happens when you wake up during the night or early in the morning—do you have trouble falling back asleep, or does it feel like you were never really asleep to begin with?

Usually I’ll wake up to some little noise in the house, nothing major, and then it’s like I’m… not fully able to settle back down. Sometimes I do drift off again, but it feels light, like I was never really sleeping deeply in the first place. And then I’m awake before the alarm anyway, feeling like I didn’t really rest. I don’t know if that answers it the right way.
Does it feel like your sleep doesn’t restore you even when you don’t wake up during the night?

Yes… I think so. I mean, even on nights where I don’t remember waking up much, I still get up before the alarm feeling like I never really rested. It’s not every single night, maybe, but it’s been a long time that sleep just feels… not very restoring. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, like feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, especially related to how you're sleeping?

Yes… I think that’s there too. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but most days it feels like the color has gone out of things a little. Even when I’m with my family at Sunday dinner, or looking at art I used to really enjoy, I’m just… not feeling it the same way. And sometimes I have to work pretty hard not to tear up, even when there isn’t a clear reason. Is that what you mean?
Do you find that these low moods or feelings of hopelessness stick around most of the day, nearly every day, even when things are going okay on the surface?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I can still go through the motions and things can look fine from the outside, but most days it’s just kind of there, that heaviness. Like the color has gone out of things a bit, even when I’m at Sunday dinner with my family or looking at art I used to really like. And I’ll find myself trying not to tear up when there isn’t really a reason. I don’t want to overstate it, but… yes, it does seem to stick around a lot of the day.
How long have you been feeling this way, with the low mood and lack of enjoyment, nearly every day?

I guess… a little over two years now. It seemed to start around when my mother-in-law moved in with us. I don’t want to blame her exactly, but that’s when I first noticed it becoming more of an almost everyday thing. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed a change in your energy level or felt unusually fatigued, even when you’re not doing much physically?

Yes… I have noticed that. I mean, I’m getting through work, so I don’t want to sound like I’m falling apart, but by the time I finish seeing my home-health clients and then come back to help at home, my body just feels really heavy. Even little things like charting my notes or folding laundry can feel like a lot to push through. Is that the kind of fatigue you mean?
